messages:
From: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@acerohealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Price <daniel.price@acerohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit C redline + adjacency behavior question

Evelyn —

Thanks for the draft order form. I've attached a redline of Exhibit C with our suggested edits (ACERO_OrderForm_ExhibitC_v3.docx). Primary concern from procurement and legal: the new "volume adjacency" paragraph in Section 2.3 changes how usage moves between SKU tiers when customers reclassify usage mid-month. The language as written can cause an inadvertent (and material) increase to our minimum committed spend if a customer bumps usage into a higher-priced SKU and then back down in the same month.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether the adjacency calc is intended to be per-invoice-period or per-billing-window (i.e., does it net within the month)?
- If the intent is to protect Redwood's revenue, can we get a commercial carveout instead of automatic floor triggers?

We flagged explicit alternate wording inline (see comments). Happy to hop on a short call — Dan (cc'd) is procurement lead.

Thanks,
Lisa Moreno
Head of Procurement, AceroHealth

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Exhibit C redline + adjacency behavior question

Lisa —

Appreciate the careful review and the redline. Short answers up front: the adjacency calc we proposed was intended to net within the invoice period (monthly), not to lock customers into a temporary higher minimum due to intra-period spikes. If the current wording reads otherwise, that's our mistake.

Quick thoughts:
- We can replace the ambiguous paragraph with a clear monthly-netting rule that preserves Redwood's ability to protect revenue from persistent up-steps while avoiding one-off spike penalties.
- Commercial carveout is reasonable for long-tail enterprise migrations; Marissa, can you propose a limited-term waiver language (e.g., first 60 days of migration) and whether that affects capacity commitments?
- Ben, FYI for billing engine implications — this could affect how we compute prorates and the true-up.

I'm copying a short list of proposed next steps in the doc and will put together a clean text suggestion (inline) by EOD so legal can review. If Acero wants to talk through scenarios, we can set a 30-min slot next week.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

Lisa / Evelyn —

Thanks for surfacing this. From a commercial standpoint, Acero's ask makes sense: we don't want short-lived spikes to trigger a durable minimum increase. Proposed commercial compromise:

1) Monthly netting: administra- tion of adjacency will net usage within the invoice period before applying any floor.
2) Migration grace: for the first 45 days after SKU migration (documented via a mutual change note), we will hold off on floor enforcement for migration-related usage that clearly traces to a migration.
3) Persistent bump trigger: if netted up-steps exceed 25% for three consecutive invoice periods, the new floor will take effect prospectively.

If Acero is comfortable, we can add these bullets as a short Annex to Exhibit C rather than changing the core definition. That keeps the order form tidy and gives both teams an operational playbook. I've attached a simple matrix that maps sample-month scenarios to outcomes (volume-adjacency-matrix.xlsx).

Next for legal: Evelyn / Ben, if you can propose redline text for the Annex, we can circulate and lock.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Exhibit C redline + adjacency behavior question

Evelyn / team —

I pulled this into the product/billing thread to make sure the implementation won't create rounding or sequencing issues. Notes below and a compact proposed replacement for the problematic paragraph.

Implementation notes:
- Monthly-netting is straightforward: aggregate tokens/embeddings per invoice period, apply tier thresholds to the neted volume, then compute prorated charges.
- Migration grace requires a mutually signed change note to mark the migration window; without that artifact we can't reliably separate migration noise from organic spikes.
- The 25% persistent bump threshold is implementable but should be calendarized (e.g., calendar months vs. 30-day rolling). Recommend calendar months to align with invoicing.

Proposed replacement text (for insertion into Exhibit C Annex):
"For purposes of applying tier thresholds and minimum commitments, Redwood will net Usage across the invoice period prior to determining the applicable tier. Usage attributable to a documented SKU migration will be exempt from floor enforcement for a migration grace period of 45 calendar days following execution of a mutually signed migration notice. If, after monthly netting, Usage exceeds the customer's current tier by more than twenty-five percent (25%) for three (3) consecutive invoice periods, Redwood may prospectively adjust the customer's minimum commitment to the tier consistent with the observed Usage. Adjustments shall apply only prospectively and shall not be retroactive to prior invoice periods."

If legal is good with this language, I can hand it to Ben to validate rounding and to engineering to generate a test vector.

-Karthik
Director, Product Engineering, Redwood Inference
